title: Securities Dealing Policy
date_approved: 18 April 2018 (Board last amended; first approved 29 September 2010)

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: All executive and non-executive directors of the Company and its subsidiaries. Subject to the black-out periods, the three-month short-term dealing ban, the section 5 additional restrictions (advance written notice and written clearance acknowledgement from the Chairman or Company Secretary), the hedging regime and the margin lending prohibition.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: must give advance written notice to, and receive written clearance acknowledgement from, the Chairman of the Audit Governance and Risk Management Committee.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: Employees who are members of the Executive Leadership Team, and/or receive performance rights under any Group Performance Rights Plan, and/or hold a position which makes them a 'director or officer' of any Group company under the Corporations Act. Subject to the same additional restrictions as Directors, with clearance from the MD & CEO or Company Secretary, plus the express ban on hedging unexercised performance rights and transfer-restricted shares.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All employees of the Company and its subsidiaries. Subject to the black-out periods and the three-month short-term dealing ban, but not to the section 5 clearance, hedging or margin lending provisions: 'At any time other than during a black-out period Employees (other than Directors and Executives) may deal in securities in the Company but only if you do not have inside information.'

definitions.hedging_definition: For the purposes of this policy, hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company and includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences.

windows.end_anchor: the day of the announcement of the Company's half year results (released in February), inclusive
the day of the announcement of the Company's full year results (released in August), inclusive

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may designate any other period as a black-out period; it is advised to Employees by Company-wide email and posted to the Company intranet, so ad hoc black-outs are notified rather than confidential. Separately, the Company may notify in writing that certain other companies' securities cannot be traded for a specified period.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not regulated as such, but a purchased put and written call over a Company shareholding fall within the hedging definition ('any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding'), which expressly extends to OTC instruments such as equity swaps and CFDs with no venue limitation. Directors may therefore enter them subject to section 5.1 advance written notice and written clearance acknowledgement, outside a black-out period and free of price sensitive information.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: in compliance with section 5.1 above; and providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Same position as Directors, with clearance from the MD & CEO or Company Secretary. Only shares that have been acquired on exercise of performance rights and are no longer subject to a transfer restriction are available.
rules.evidence: Executives must give advance notice and receive clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the MD & CEO or Company Secretary before commencing to deal in Company Securities

rules.detail: Section 5, which contains the hedging and margin lending provisions, applies only to Directors and Executives. For other Employees the Policy regulates only black-out period trading and short-term dealing, and does not address derivatives.

Hedging of shareholdings is expressly permitted for Directors provided section 5.1 clearance is obtained and the hedge is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out while in possession of price sensitive information. Each of entry, renewal, alteration and close-out is a separate compliance event. The Policy imposes no unvested-rights restriction on Directors because performance rights are an Executive construct.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: in compliance with section 5.1 above; and providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Executives may hedge shareholdings on the same terms as Directors once the shares are held free of any transfer restriction, with clearance from the MD & CEO or Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: in compliance with section 5.1 above

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging performance rights granted under a Plan before exercise, with no clearance or exemption route.
rules.evidence: However, Executives are not permitted to hedge performance rights granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights

rules.detail: The ban continues after exercise for as long as the resulting securities are subject to a transfer restriction, so shares in a holding lock cannot form part of a collar.
rules.evidence: or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction

rules.detail: The hedging provision sits in section 5 'Additional Restrictions on Directors and Executives' and is not extended to other Employees.

Monetisation structures are not named. A prepaid forward or similar limits the economic risk of a Company security holding and so is hedging permitted with clearance, but section 4.3 gives 'forward contracts' as an example of prohibited short-term dealings, so a forward-based monetisation of short tenor is at risk of being caught by the short-term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned. A short position that limits the economic risk of a holding would fall within the hedging definition for Directors and Executives; a naked short would also engage the three-month sell-and-buy prohibition.
Securities lending is not named and the dealing description in section 3.1 is limited to buying, selling, subscribing and agreements to do so.

CFDs are expressly named as an example of hedging, so they are permitted for Directors and Executives on the hedging conditions (section 5.1 clearance, no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out) and prohibited over unexercised performance rights and transfer-restricted shares.
rules.evidence: includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences

rules.detail: The hedging section does not apply to Employees below Director and Executive level.
Flat prohibition on entering into a margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities. No approval, hardship or exemption route, and no distinction by security state.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Same flat prohibition as for Directors.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending prohibition is confined to Directors and Executives; other Employees are not addressed.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not named, and the section 3.1 description of trading or dealing does not extend to encumbrances. Only encumbrance under a margin lending arrangement is caught, and only for Directors and Executives.

The Policy prohibits only margin lending arrangements; it contains no general prohibition on secured financing, loans or other financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, and does not define 'margin lending arrangement'. A conventional term loan secured on Company shares, without margining or a mark-to-market top-up mechanic, is therefore not expressly caught, but the wider the lender's collateral-maintenance and enforcement rights, the closer the facility comes to the prohibited category.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy Company securities within a three-month period, nor enter into any other short-term dealings, with forward contracts given as an example. No carve-outs are stated, although section 4.4 permits exercise of vested performance rights within a black-out period.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (so the Company can inform ASX)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately (notice is expressed as advance written notice when they buy or sell shares)
clearance.evidence: Directors (other than the Chairman of the Board) must give advance written notice and receive written clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the Chairman or Company Secretary before commencing to deal in Company Securities

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Audit Governance and Risk Management Committee
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (so the Company can inform ASX)
clearance.evidence: The Chairman of the Board must give advance written notice and receive written clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the Chairman of the Audit Governance and Risk Management Committee before commencing to deal in Company Securities
Directors and Executives who are given written clearance to deal in accordance with the Policy must deal as soon as possible and in any event within 5 business days of the clearance being received.
At any time other than during a black-out period Employees (other than Directors and Executives) may deal in securities in the Company but only if you do not have inside information.

short_term.basis: buy and sell or sell and buy within a three-month period; also any other short-term dealing, e.g. forward contracts
short_term.evidence: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).

exceptions.evidence: Where you are not in possession of price sensitive information and there exists exceptional circumstances such as severe financial difficulties or passive trades (such as sales compelled by law) you may apply in writing to the Company Secretary for approval to dispose of (but not to acquire) Company securities during a black-out period.
passive trades (such as sales compelled by law)

exceptions.approver: MD & CEO or Company Secretary for any sale during a black-out period
exceptions.evidence: Vested performance rights held pursuant to a Plan may be exercised in accordance with the relevant Plan rules. The exercise of performance rights may occur within a black-out period.

exemption_authority: Section 4.2: the Company Secretary may approve disposals (but not acquisitions) of Company securities during a black-out period where the applicant has no price sensitive information and there are exceptional circumstances such as severe financial difficulties or passive trades; approvals are valid for three business days. Section 4.4: the MD & CEO or Company Secretary may give written permission for a sale of shares acquired on exercise of performance rights during a black-out period. There is no authority to waive the margin lending prohibition or the ban on hedging unexercised performance rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: in compliance with section 5.1 above; and providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually for an ASX policy, the collar's derivative legs over vested unrestricted shares are affirmatively permitted rather than banned, subject only to clearance and the inside information test.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every roll, restrike, partial unwind and termination of the collar is a separate compliance event, so the bank cannot rely on unilateral adjustment rights and must build in the executive's ability to stand still while in possession of price sensitive information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company and includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is drafted by economic effect rather than instrument or venue, so an OTC put and call package with a bank is plainly within it and cannot be structured around.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funding leg is the only real obstacle: 'margin lending arrangement' is not defined, so a loan secured on the collared shares should be documented as a fixed-term facility without margin calls or collateral top-up, and written confirmation obtained from the Company Secretary that it is not caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Executives are not permitted to hedge performance rights granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collateral pool must be limited to shares that have been exercised and released from any transfer restriction; the bank should require evidence of that status at trade date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance under this clause is not an endorsement of proposed trading and it is the Directors and Executives whom are ultimately responsible for ensuring their dealings in securities comply with the applicable laws and as applicable, the Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar gives the bank no comfort that the Company has assessed the structure against the margin lending or short-term dealing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealing means the collar and any associated funding should have a tenor comfortably beyond three months and no early-termination triggers within it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to all executive and non-executive directors (Directors) and all employees (Employees) of the Company and its subsidiaries (the Group).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy has no associates or connected persons clause, so on its face a collar entered by a family trust or controlled entity is not directly caught, although the executive's own conduct in procuring the dealing remains subject to the insider trading provisions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: for any other period designated as a black-out period by the Board and advised to the Employees.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ad hoc black-outs are communicated by Company-wide email and intranet rather than kept confidential, so the executive can at least tell the bank that a dealing window is unavailable.

summary: Aurizon is one of the more permissive ASX policies for the derivative legs of a collar: section 5.2 expressly permits Directors and Executives to hedge their shareholdings, and the hedging definition reaches any transaction, arrangement or financial product limiting the economic risk of a Company holding, including OTC instruments such as equity swaps and CFDs. The conditions are section 5.1 advance written notice and written clearance acknowledgement (Chairman or Company Secretary for Directors, the Audit Governance and Risk Management Committee Chairman for the Chairman, the MD & CEO or Company Secretary for Executives), dealing within 5 business days of clearance, outside the 1 January and 1 July black-out periods and any Board-designated black-out, and no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out. The collar cannot cover unexercised performance rights or shares still subject to a transfer restriction, and its tenor should exceed three months given the short-term dealing ban that expressly names forward contracts. The funding leg is the pinch point: section 5.3 prohibits Directors and Executives entering any margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities, but there is no general secured financing, encumbrance or pledge prohibition and no definition of margin lending, so a fixed-term loan secured on the collared shares without margin calls or collateral maintenance is arguably outside the ban and should be confirmed in writing with the Company Secretary before documentation. The Policy is silent on forced sales, financing disclosure and any minimum shareholding, so those risks must be managed contractually rather than by reference to the Policy.
